articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft dropped a record-breaking 200 patches this Patch Tuesday because apparently they've been collecting vulnerabilities like Pokémon cards. Three dozen earned the coveted 'critical' rating, which in Microsoft-speak means 'we're really sorry about this one.'

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters found a sweet Oracle ERP zero-day and decided to make American universities their personal data piñata. Because nothing says 'higher education' like getting schooled by ransomware gangs.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages got hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits. The irony of Arch users getting pwned while telling everyone they use Arch is absolutely *chef's kiss*.

articles.title: Agentjacking Attack Tricks AI Coding Agents Into Running Malicious Code
articles.summary: Chinese hackers spent nearly a decade backdooring Linux PAM and OpenSSH login systems like the world's most patient burglars. Sometimes the best place to hide is exactly where everyone's looking but nobody's seeing.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub because apparently 'security agency' doesn't automatically mean 'secure.' Congress is asking the hard questions while we're all just facepalming.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702 surveillance authority finally expired, and EFF is throwing a well-deserved victory party. Sometimes the best defense against government spying is simply letting their own bureaucracy trip over itself.

articles.title: NanoClaw now armed with JFrog for safer packages
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries finally grew a spine and rallied Democrats against extending domestic spy laws. Better late than never, but we'll take principled opposition to surveillance overreach wherever we can get it.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Uses Oracle Zero-Day to Rampage Higher Ed
articles.summary: Congress rushed through a 'technical reorganization' bill that fundamentally rewrites copyright law because nothing says 'transparency' like hiding massive legal changes in boring committee names. The EFF is rightfully pissed.

articles.title: ICE Should Show It Hasn’t Been “Infiltrated by Violent Extremists,” Senator Urges
articles.summary: Indiana banned press from executions under the guise of 'dignity' but really just wants to kill people in secret. There's nothing dignified about state-sanctioned murder hidden from public scrutiny.

articles.title: CISA orders federal agencies to “patch smarter”
articles.summary: CISA's new BOD 26-04 directive forces federal agencies to patch critical vulns in just three days using a fancy four-variable risk model. Finally, some bureaucrats who understand that 'eventually' isn't a timeline.
